blocks.text: Fresh palm wine is sweet. Left standing, yeast turns its sugar into alcohol. Left longer, bacteria turn that alcohol into vinegar. Two functional groups, appearing one after the other in the same calabash, and both are on the WAEC syllabus.

blocks.title: Functional group
blocks.text: A functional group is the atom or group of atoms that gives a family of organic compounds its characteristic chemical properties. Alkanols contain the hydroxyl group -OH and have the general formula CnH2n+1OH. Alkanoic acids contain the carboxyl group -COOH and have the general formula CnH2n+1COOH.

blocks.caption: The oxygen-containing families and their functional groups

blocks.markdown:
## Ethanol

Ethanol, C2H5OH, is the alcohol in palm wine, beer and burukutu. It boils at 78 degrees Celsius, well above ethane, because hydrogen bonding between the -OH groups of neighbouring molecules must be overcome.

### Preparation by fermentation

Starch from cassava, maize or millet is first broken down to glucose. Yeast then supplies the enzyme zymase, which converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide in the absence of air:

C6H12O6 -> 2C2H5OH + 2CO2

The optimum temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius. Fermentation stops naturally at roughly 14 percent ethanol, because higher concentrations kill the yeast. Fractional distillation then concentrates the ethanol.

blocks.title: Ethanol to ethanoic acid
blocks.prompt: Describe how ethanol can be converted to ethanoic acid in the laboratory, and explain why palm wine turns sour if left in an open container.

steps.text: In the laboratory, warm ethanol with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution, an oxidising agent, under reflux.
The alcohol is oxidised in two stages, first to ethanal and then to ethanoic acid: CH3CH2OH -> CH3CHO -> CH3COOH.
The colour of the mixture changes from orange to green as dichromate(VI) is reduced to chromium(III), which is a useful sign that oxidation has occurred.
Refluxing rather than simple heating is essential, because ethanal boils at only 21 degrees Celsius and would otherwise escape before it could be oxidised further.
In palm wine the same overall oxidation happens naturally. Airborne bacteria of the genus Acetobacter use atmospheric oxygen to oxidise the ethanol to ethanoic acid.
That is why an open calabash sours: the wine has effectively become dilute vinegar.

blocks.answer: Oxidise with warm acidified potassium dichromate(VI) under reflux; in palm wine, Acetobacter bacteria do the same job with atmospheric oxygen

blocks.markdown:
## Reactions of ethanol

- **Combustion**: C2H5OH + 3O2 -> 2CO2 + 3H2O, burning with a clean blue flame
- **With sodium**: 2C2H5OH + 2Na -> 2C2H5ONa + H2, giving sodium ethoxide and hydrogen. The reaction is much gentler than sodium with water
- **Oxidation**: to ethanoic acid, as above
- **Dehydration**: with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid at 170 degrees Celsius, water is removed to give ethene
- **Esterification**: with an alkanoic acid to give an ester

## Reactions of ethanoic acid

Ethanoic acid is a weak acid, only partially ionised, but it shows all the normal reactions of an acid.

- With a metal: 2CH3COOH + Mg -> (CH3COO)2Mg + H2
- With a base: CH3COOH + NaOH -> CH3COONa + H2O
- With a carbonate: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 -> 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2

blocks.title: Esterification
blocks.text: An alkanol reacts with an alkanoic acid, warmed with a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid as catalyst, to give an ester and water. CH3COOH + C2H5OH <=> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. The ester ethyl ethanoate has a sweet fruity smell, and esters are responsible for the flavours of many fruits and are used in perfumes.

blocks.title: Distinguishing the two families
blocks.text: Add sodium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV) solution to each sample. The alkanoic acid fizzes and releases carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky; the alkanol does nothing. Both react with sodium metal to give hydrogen, so that test alone will not separate them.

points: Alkanols contain the -OH group; alkanoic acids contain the -COOH group.
Hydrogen bonding between -OH groups makes alkanols boil much higher than the corresponding alkanes.
Fermentation of glucose by the enzyme zymase in yeast gives ethanol and carbon dioxide.
Oxidising ethanol with acidified dichromate(VI) gives ethanal and then ethanoic acid, with orange changing to green.
Ethanoic acid is a weak acid but reacts normally with metals, bases and carbonates.
An alkanol plus an alkanoic acid with a concentrated acid catalyst gives a sweet-smelling ester and water.
